hypotheses.justification: The conclusion mentions neither hu nor u. hu is only used in the proof to build ⟨u,hu⟩ : ↥B. It follows from hcov and hT1, so it can be dropped. Here S := s9cIndHom (s9cOfN hA hB t), and s9cIndHom_mk / s9c3_map_mk say S (mk y) = mk (t *ᵥ y) for y ∈ B. Since S ≠ 1, extensionality plus Submodule.Quotient.induction_on gives y ∈ B with mk (t*ᵥy) ≠ mk y in B ⧸ A.comap B.subtype. That means t*ᵥy - y ∉ A. By hcov, t*ᵥy - y = c • u. Here c ≠ 0, because otherwise the difference is 0 ∈ A. Also t*ᵥy ∈ B by s9cFlag_mapB, so t*ᵥy - y ∈ B. Therefore u = c⁻¹ • (t*ᵥy - y) ∈ B. The rest of the proof is unchanged. The theorem is true without hu, with no degenerate case needed. Deleting hu is fine while huA is kept, and huA can also be deleted at the same time (see below).

The conclusion does not mention huA, and it is derivable from hT1. Suppose u ∈ A. Then, by hcov, t*ᵥv - v = c • u ∈ A for every v. For y ∈ B this gives mk (t*ᵥy) = mk y in the quotient B ⧸ A.comap B.subtype. By s9cIndHom_mk, S = s9cIndHom (s9cOfN hA hB t) then fixes every class. Hence S = 1, which contradicts hT1. So u ∉ A follows. The rest of the proof (hu0, hsub, finrank comparison) goes through once this fact is derived inside the proof. The theorem is true without huA. This argument does not use hu. huA can be deleted on its own, and also together with hu: the derivation of hu above uses only hcov and hT1, not huA.
